title: Dizzy and Billy Eckstine's band at Club Sudan
summary: Butler led the relief band at Club Sudan where Eckstine's band of future bebop names tried out chords behind his singing until he threatened to disband.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: You see, these things -- now, after I had heard --
Dizzy, Dizzy, Dizzy -- my man. He's my man. Dizzy's my man.
And then, they were in the -- what's this man's band?
No, they were in Billy Eckstine's band.
And they was getting straight while Billy was singing. You see, my man was singing and somebody's
back there trying out them chords --

That's an awful feeling. So, they was working at a place called Club Sudan (phonetic). I was in the relief band. I was up there singing the blues and I had a little short trumpet up there and we was swinging pretty good too.
They had some beautiful musicians -- they had Fats up there, they had Dizzy, they had everybody who was anybody. What's that young boy, Sir Charles somebody?

On the baritone -- oh, he had everything up there. And Eckstine was out front looking beautiful and singing but it seems like everytime Eckstine would try to sing, somebody up in that trumpet section was trying to get together.
So, it seems though Eckstine says 'Look, I'm up here trying to make it and I keep hearing a lot of stuff and their names are not out front.

'If I get out here by myself, ain't nothing going to happen to me. I want you all to know that.' So, seems like -- and to prove it, Eckstine, he was supposed to get off every Monday. We was playing and Eckstine, he had, we played his music and it broke the house up. Had a standing ovation.
So, and he made one of the saxophone players stay
there because he got drunk and laid off a night before so he had, he's -- he had to sit down in his chair and he listened to it.

He told, now, 'You see there -- nothing happens to me, I'm Eckstine, that's the sound, now, you all up there getting straight, now, you are going to have to get straight somewhere else because I'm going to disband now.'
